clue.text: At first sight, a strange sort of pacifier mother inserted

indicators.note: the word for mother is placed inside the rearranged letters
a strange sort of something is an odd version of it, so the letters of pacifier are rearranged

parts.note: Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone glimpses an odd kind of dummy that a mother has popped into a baby's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pacifier' suggests a baby's dummy, but it is only fodder for 'strange sort of'; 'inserted' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used to mean on initial impression, before closer examination.

clue.text: Engineers have aeroplane part for sale

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
the tail is the rear section of an aircraft

explanation.surface: Engineers have a bit of an aircraft to sell off.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods offered in a shop to the public are sold at the counter, so the word describes things being sold.

clue.text: Damage one yellow blossom

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
I is the Roman numeral for one
gold is a yellow colour

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a single yellow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common garden flower with orange or yellow heads, an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Open warfare

definitions.meaning: something open to anyone, with no restrictions on who takes part
a chaotic brawl or fight in which everyone joins in

explanation.definitionFit: An unrestricted event is open to all comers, and a melee where everyone fights is the same term used for a general brawl.

clue.text: Choral work may bring two armies together

parts.note: can and may both express being able or permitted
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve, and two of them give the abbreviation twice
the second Territorial Army of the pair

explanation.surface: A piece of music for choir might unite two military forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve, so 'two armies' gives its abbreviation twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bach-style composition for voices and orchestra, sung by a choir and soloists, is a choral piece.

clue.text: Seed gets a hidden advantage

indicators.note: the letters are concealed within the run of the words Seed gets

explanation.surface: A seed acquires a secret benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a slight lead over a rival is having the upper hand, a small superiority.

clue.text: Girl carrying one 'ulking' instrument

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the numeral inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: Olga is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one
hulking means huge, and the apostrophe shows the H is dropped, leaving UGE

explanation.surface: A girl lugs a single enormous device about.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ulking' signals a dropped H, so the synonym HUGE loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipstick-style meter in a car engine measures lubricant level, a measuring device.

clue.text: Desire nice sort of divorce

indicators.note: a sort of something is a loose version of it, so the letters of desire nice are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone wants a pleasant kind of marriage break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the letters of DESIRE NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the provisional court order in English law that ends a marriage unless cause is shown within a set period.

clue.text: Canyon subject to pollution

definitions.meaning: a narrow pass or gorge between hills
to make dirty or desecrate something

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow gorge is a noun sense, and to sully or pollute is the verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: The way to encourage fish

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Advice on how to cheer on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bony fish whose eggs are eaten as caviar.

clue.text: Generate trouble for an adolescent

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of generate are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Bringing about difficulties for a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen is a youth going through puberty.

clue.text: Historian can look into 'old sources

indicators.note: the sources of words are their beginnings, so the first letter of each of can, look, into and old is taken

explanation.surface: A historian may investigate ancient documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly she is the Muse of history, patron of historians, rather than a historian herself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Muse presides over history and is pictured recording past events.

clue.text: Example of the flora and fauna turning up in secluded spot

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for the secluded spot

parts.note: a corner is a quiet, out-of-the-way place

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a wolf is an example of fauna, an animal

explanation.surface: Some plant and animal life emerges in a quiet nook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flora and fauna' reads as one phrase, but 'Example of the flora' is the definition and 'fauna' alone supplies an animal, turned up because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-flowered plant of fields is one specimen of plant life.

clue.text: Roof is free

definitions.meaning: the roof is the part found atop a building
given without charge, paid for by the establishment

explanation.definitionFit: A roof sits atop the building, and a drink given free by the landlord is said to be paid for by the pub.

clue.text: Give Italy, with its extremes of climate, a new resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so these letters are put into a fresh order
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Italy, with its varied weather, would make a fresh holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort: ITALY, ITS and CE (first and last letters of climate) are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Give as a noun means stretchiness or springiness, the ability to bend and recover.

clue.text: One working for the Highways Department, or possibly a copywriter

definitions.text: One working for the Highways Department

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the two letters of or

parts.note: an adman writes advertising copy

explanation.surface: Someone who repairs highways, or perhaps writes advertisements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or possibly' looks like a link offering an alternative job, but 'possibly' is the anagram signal for the two letters of 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer who maintains public streets and highways.

clue.text: Scholar not in practice

definitions.meaning: a university teacher or learned person
theoretical rather than practical, of no real consequence

explanation.definitionFit: A university lecturer is a learned person, and a merely theoretical point is one with no practical relevance.

clue.text: Flower of extraordinary size a doctor introduced

indicators.note: the two pieces are put inside the rearranged letters
something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters of size are rearranged

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A remarkably large bloom is brought in by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows, a river, not a bloom. 'extraordinary' signals the anagram and 'introduced' the container; the S comes from the clue's 'size'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is a thing that flows, a river; this one is in southern Africa.

clue.text: Without cream, a dessert it is easy to slip up on

definitions.text: it is easy to slip up on

parts.note: black coffee is served without cream or milk
an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: Without cream, this pudding is one you could easily trip over.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin transparent frozen water on a road surface is notoriously slippery.

clue.text: A good reason for being on the beach

parts.note: grounds are a good reason or basis for something

explanation.surface: Someone has a valid excuse for lounging by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run onto the shore is stranded, beached on land.

clue.text: Torch left burnt residue in the passage

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the word for the passage

parts.note: a flight is a passage through the air, or a flight of stairs
ash is what is left after burning

explanation.surface: A torch has left soot behind it in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'passage' is a flight, as of stairs or through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery lamp held in the hand; in British usage a torch.

clue.text: Worker — one opposed to …

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A labourer who is set against something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sentence on into the next clue; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a preposition meaning against.

clue.text: Went first into excessively Spanish city

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: too means excessively
led means went first, in front

explanation.surface: Someone went too far ahead into a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic city in central Spain famous for its swords.

clue.text: … a few of the first clues

definitions.meaning: the puzzle's opening clues are numbered 1 and 2

explanation.definitionFit: A small number is a couple or so, and the first two clue numbers are literally the numbers that open the list.

clue.text: Catch split up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to part is to split or separate

explanation.surface: A snag has torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare that catches animals; to trap is to catch.

clue.text: Till name is deleted, is man in employment?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is removed from the word meaning till

parts.note: until means till
taken as written
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A question about whether a shop employee is still on the payroll once his name is struck off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like a cash register but means UNTIL; 'deleted' removes N, leaving UTIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put to use is being employed, so in employment.

clue.text: A mysterious character, girl holding one award for gallantry

indicators.note: the girl's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one
GM is the George Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: A puzzling person: a girl who has won a single bravery medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone baffling and inscrutable is a puzzle of a person.

clue.text: Wallaby requires rice and fruit.

parts.note: paddy is rice, especially in the husk or growing in the field
a melon is a fruit

explanation.surface: A small kangaroo needs a diet of rice and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian marsupial species, a small type of kangaroo.
